chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The woman in ihram should not look in the mirror for adornment."

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And she should not anoint herself with fragrant perfume, and anoint with oil, and with sheeraj (sesame oil) and butter if she wishes. And it is not permissible to use oils that contain fragrance before entering ihram if their scent remains after ihram. And there is no harm in using other oils that do not contain fragrance in that state, and after the ghusl for ihram as long as she has not entered ihram. So when she enters ihram, all oils become forbidden upon her, unless she is compelled to use them, for then she uses that which does not contain fragrance, such as sheeraj and butter.

key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمَةُ: The woman in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a woman in ihram regarding mirrors and perfumed oils?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elaborates on this narration by distinguishing between the prohibition of applying fragrant oils during ihram and the permissibility of non-fragrant oils like sesame oil and butter, noting that all oils become prohibited only after the formal declaration of ihram unless compulsion arises. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the purity of the ritual state and the specific conditions under which adornment is restricted to maintain spiritual focus. The text underscores the practical application of these rules, ensuring pilgrims avoid lingering scents that might distract from the solemnity of the pilgrimage.
